name: Aon plc

listing.hq: Dublin, Ireland (company-stated principal executive office; PitchBook lists London)

corporate_actions.event: Agreed to acquire USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17.0bn cash ($16.7bn net of tax attributes, ~14.5x synergised TTM adj EBITDA); debt-funded; expected close Q4-2026 subject to regulatory approval. Aon is ACQUIRER (not a G6 target).
Acquired NFP (~$13bn) - middle-market US broker/benefits platform

geography.fx_notes: Irish-domiciled, global (120+ countries). Exact 10-K geographic split not extracted in this pass (not disclosed here). NFP (2024) and USI (pending, ~$3bn US revenue) raise US weight materially (INFERENCE).

kpis.name: Q3-26 organic: Risk Capital / Human Capital
Net market impact (rate & exposure) on organic
kpis.value: 'slightly positive', within expected 0-2pt range despite softer pricing

kpis.name: Leverage (company definition)
kpis.value: 2.9x end-2025 -> ~4.5x at USI close; target 2.8-3.0x within 24 months

kpis.name: Gross debt / EBITDA (provider)
kpis.value: ~4.3x (PitchBook TTM 3Q26 total debt $28.9bn incl. leases & pre-funded USI debt / EBITDA $6.7bn)

company_fcf.definition: Company FCF = cash from operations less capex

acquisitions.notes: USI: $17.0bn gross; ~14.5x synergised TTM adj EBITDA (pre-synergy multiple higher, not disclosed); funded by new debt incl. ~$4bn term loan A; Aon to repay USI's ~$4.4bn debt at close
NFP ~$13bn (cash + stock + assumed debt; exact split not extracted)

management.senior_turnover_5y: CEO stable since 2005; CFO change 2023 (Christa Davies -> Edmund Reese, not re-verified)
management.succession_notes: Long-tenured CEO; no announced succession plan found - key-person risk
management.guidance_record: '3x3' plan final year 2026; management reaffirmed organic, margin, EPS and FCF guidance in Q3-26 (S2); FY25 'achieved all full-year objectives' (S5)

guidance.value: mid-single-digit or greater organic growth; 70-80bp adj operating margin expansion; adj EPS growth; double-digit FCF growth
accretive to adj EPS in 2028 and thereafter; no near-term buybacks

evidence: Commercial risk, reinsurance and benefits brokerage are annually renewing (S1)
A.rationale: Highly recurring broking/benefits revenue with stable organic growth.

evidence: Treaty reinsurance grew with new business and retention despite lower rates (S2)
B.rationale: Top-3 global broker with reinsurance and analytics depth; switching costs for large clients.

C.rationale: Aon Business Services platform delivers operating leverage; margins among the highest of global brokers (INFERENCE).

D.rationale: Moderate organic runway; middle-market push depends on executing two large integrations.

E.rationale: Balanced developed-market spread, but US weight rising with NFP/USI; exact split not extracted.

F.rationale: Long, credible delivery record; CEO tenure 21 years raises succession risk.

evidence: USI $17bn at ~14.5x synergised EBITDA, fully debt-funded (S3)
Leverage ~4.5x at close; S&P outlook to negative; buybacks suspended (S4)
G.rationale: Two consecutive large, high-multiple, debt-funded deals (NFP, USI) before returns are evidenced; balance-sheet stretched.

H.rationale: Standard governance; not reviewed in depth.

evidence: AI-enabled Aon Business Services cited for lower unit costs (S2)
I1.rationale: Large-account broking resilient; Human Capital/benefits admin more automatable - moderate (INFERENCE).

I2.rationale: Revenue not tied to AI capex.

evidence: ABS platform delivering operating leverage and lower unit costs (S2)
Net market impact slightly positive, within 0-2pt range, despite softer pricing (S2)
J.rationale: Limited dependence on rate cycle; fiduciary income sensitive to rates.

evidence: Heavy restructuring/integration adjustments around NFP and USI (S2,S3)
K.rationale: Adjusted vs GAAP gap will widen with USI transaction and integration costs.

ai.notes: No identified revenue tied to AI/data-centre capex; AI used for ABS productivity (S2).

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: Company states net market impact (rate & exposure) was 'slightly positive' and within a 0-2pt range in Q3-26 (S2), implying ~4-6pts of the 6% organic came from new business/retention (INFERENCE from company commentary).

gates.notes: G1 = B: company guides leverage ~4.5x at USI close (> 4.0x broker threshold) with dated path to 2.8-3.0x within 24 months (S4); PitchBook TTM gross debt/EBITDA already ~4.3x on pre-funded debt. G6 = C: Aon is the acquirer (USI pending close Q4-26), not a takeover target; acquisition is large (~$3bn revenue vs Aon ~$17.7bn) - monitor. G4 not computed here; FCF $3.2bn vs NI ~$3.7bn 2025 (PitchBook) suggests >80% conversion.

bull_points: Most consistent organic growth among global brokers (6% three years running) with management stating rate is only a 0-2pt contributor.
USI + NFP create a scaled US middle-market platform on Aon's ABS cost engine; synergies could drive double-digit FCF growth from 2028.
High FCF conversion supports rapid deleveraging (repaid $1.9bn debt in 2025).
bear_points: Leverage ~4.5x after a $17bn debt-funded deal at ~14.5x synergised EBITDA (higher pre-synergy); S&P outlook negative; buybacks paused.
Integration risk of two large US acquisitions in three years; middle-market producer attrition is a known post-deal risk.
Long-tenured CEO (since 2005) without public succession plan.
thesis_breakers: Leverage not back below 3.5x by end-2027 (company target 2.8-3.0x within 24 months of close).
Organic growth below 4% for a full year.
